# SIGNAL

Broadcasts a named signal that releases every entity waiting at a HOLD block for it, for example a shift start, a gate opening or a green light.

After an optional delay, succeeds the named signal event (releasing every HOLD block currently waiting on it) and immediately replaces it with a fresh one -- broadcast, edge-triggered, auto-reset.

Family: control. Python builder: `m.signal(...)`.

## Typical uses

Use SIGNAL to broadcast an event that releases entities waiting at [HOLD](hold.md) blocks: a shift start, a green light, a truck arrival. Send a dummy entity through it from a CREATE on a schedule, or let a real entity trigger it as it passes. To release entities on a state of the model, use a HOLD in `Condition` mode with no SIGNAL.

## Behaviour and rules

After its optional delay, the block fires the signal named `signal_name`. Every HOLD that is waiting on that name at that moment is released. The signal then resets at once. It is a broadcast that fires on a single edge, so it has no memory.

An entity that reaches a HOLD after the signal has fired waits for the next one. A signal that nobody waits on is lost, and there is no error. The name must match the HOLD's `signal_name` exactly.

The entity that passes through SIGNAL continues unchanged along the single outgoing link after the delay. A sampled delay below 0 is cut to 0.

## Ports

- Inputs: any number of incoming links.
- Outputs: one outgoing link.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `distribution` | str | `'Constant'` |  |  |  | Name of a registered distribution (see the distribution reference). |
| `dist_params` | dict | `{'value': 0.0}` |  | time | `time_unit` | Parameters for `distribution`, by name (e.g. {"rate": 0.5} for Exponential). |
| `time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit the sampled duration is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit, no conversion) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `signal_name` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of the signal to succeed; matches a HOLD block's signal_name. |

## Problem codes

No check names this block type.

## Example

The snippet seeds itself; its output is from a run made when this page was generated.

```python
from nagasim import build as nb

m = nb.Model(time_limit=100)
m.create("Parts", distribution=nb.Constant(value=1), max_arrivals=10) >> m.hold(signal_name="Open") >> m.dispose()
m.create("Gate", distribution=nb.Constant(value=1), max_arrivals=1, start_time=30) >> m.signal(signal_name="Open") >> m.dispose()

results = m.run(seed=1)
print(int(results.kpi("system/Total Entities Completed")), "entities completed after the SIGNAL block fired at t=30")
```

```text
11 entities completed after the SIGNAL block fired at t=30
```
